passage:
The bus stand was loud and crowded, a horn blaring every few seconds, and Nandini was tired. When the conductor handed over her ticket, her mother Rehana nudged her. "What do we say?"
"Thank you," said Nandini flatly, looking at her shoes.
Rehana did not scold. At the next stop the fruit seller passed a banana up through the window, and Rehana said warmly, "Thank you, that looks so sweet," looking straight at him. Nandini watched.
At the third stop she said it to the seller herself, with no nudge. "Thank you." This time she looked up.

qa.q: Who nudged Nandini to say thank you?
How does Nandini feel when she says 'Thank you' to the conductor?
qa.a: Tired and just going through the motions. She says it flatly and looks at her shoes.

qa.q: What choice did Rehana make instead of scolding?
qa.a: She modelled a warm thank you to the fruit seller, looking at him, so Nandini could watch how it is done.

qa.q: What might the fruit seller feel when Nandini says thank you and looks up?
qa.a: Probably pleased and noticed, since the thanks comes with eye contact.

grounding: A child says thank you because she was told to, and repetition and modelling plant the habit before the feeling.

passage:
Every morning Siddharth chirped "Thank you, bhaiya!" to the watchman without breaking stride. It came out like part of the alphabet. His mother Lakshmi noticed he never looked up.
One rainy day she slowed at the gate. "Thank you for holding the umbrella for us, bhaiya. You got wet," she said, and smiled at him. The watchman smiled back and his shoulders eased.
Siddharth stopped skipping. The next morning he said the same words, then glanced up. The watchman waved.
It wasn't feeling yet, just a small peek. Lakshmi went on saying hers aloud.

qa.q: What did Siddharth say to the watchman every morning?
What does Lakshmi seem to worry about in Siddharth's thank-yous?
qa.a: That they are only a rote phrase with no feeling yet, since he says it like part of the alphabet and never looks up.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi do to show Siddharth a different way of saying thanks?
qa.a: She slowed at the gate, named what the watchman had done and smiled at him, letting Siddharth see the effect.

qa.q: How might the watchman feel when Lakshmi thanks him for holding the umbrella?
qa.a: Seen and appreciated, since he smiles back and his shoulders ease.

grounding: A child says thank you as a habit without feeling, and modelling by an adult plants the practice.
